recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types + Employee module (foundation)
recommended_phases.rationale: Shared enums (LeaveType, LeaveStatus, EmploymentStatus, AuditAction) and BaseEntity must exist before any domain module. Employee is the root foundation module with zero domain dependencies — it only depends on shared/types and shared/db. Build the full vertical slice: model, repository interface, repository, service interface, service, barrel export.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Policy module (foundation)
recommended_phases.rationale: Policy is the second foundation module. It depends only on shared/types and shared/db. No dependency on employee. Build full vertical slice: model, repository interface, repository, service interface, service, barrel export.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Balance module (mid-layer)
recommended_phases.rationale: Balance depends on employee (to verify employee exists/is active) and policy (to look up entitlement). Both foundation modules are complete from Phases 1-2. Build full vertical slice: model, repository interface, repository, service interface, service, barrel export.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Notification + Audit modules (mid-layer, independent)
recommended_phases.rationale: Notification and Audit have zero domain-module dependencies — they only depend on shared/types and shared/db. They can be built together since they are independent of each other and of employee/policy/balance. Build both full vertical slices: model, repository interface, repository, service interface, service, barrel export for each.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: Leave module (orchestrator)
recommended_phases.rationale: Leave orchestrates all five downstream modules via constructor injection. All dependencies (employee, policy, balance, notification, audit) are complete. Build full vertical slice: model, repository interface, repository, service interface, service, barrel export. The LeaveService constructor receives IEmployeeService, IPolicyService, IBalanceService, INotificationService, IAuditService.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6: Validation schemas (all modules)
recommended_phases.rationale: Create Zod validation schemas for all six modules. Each module gets a <module>.validation.ts file. Schemas cover: leave request create/approve/reject/cancel/query, balance lookup, employee lookup, policy lookup. Depends on shared types (enums) and domain models from Phases 1-5.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 7: Controllers (all modules)
recommended_phases.rationale: Create controller classes for all six modules. Each controller receives its corresponding service interface via constructor. Controllers translate HTTP concerns (request parsing, status codes) to service calls. Depends on service interfaces and validation schemas from Phases 1-6.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 8: Routes + app registration
recommended_phases.rationale: Create route files for all six modules, register them in app.ts. Each route file instantiates its controller and service (no DI container), wires Zod validation, and applies RBAC middleware stubs. Update app.ts to register all route plugins. Depends on controllers from Phase 7.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries

- **Presentation**: Controllers + Routes (Phases 7-8). Translate HTTP to service calls. No business logic.
- **Application**: Service interfaces + implementations (Phases 1-5). Orchestrate domain operations. LeaveService is the sole orchestrator; all others are domain services.
- **Domain**: Models/entities (owned by each module). Pure data shapes with lifecycle rules live in their module; cross-module enums live in shared/types.
- **Infrastructure**: Repositories (owned by each module), db/connection.ts (shared). All DB access through repository interfaces (GP-001).

## Dependency direction (verified acyclic)

```
shared/types  ←  shared/db
     ↑              ↑
employee ──────────┘  (foundation, zero domain deps)
policy   ──────────┘  (foundation, zero domain deps)
     ↑              ↑
balance ────────────┘  (mid-layer: depends on employee + policy)
notification ───────┘  (mid-layer: zero domain deps)
audit ──────────────┘  (mid-layer: zero domain deps)
     ↑
leave ───────────────── (orchestrator: depends on all five above)
```

## Constructor injection pattern (no DI container)

LeaveService receives all five dependencies via constructor:
`new LeaveService(employeeService, policyService, balanceService, notificationService, auditService)`

BalanceService receives two:
`new BalanceService(balanceRepo, employeeService, policyService)`

All other services receive only their repository:
`new EmployeeService(employeeRepo)`, `new PolicyService(policyRepo)`, etc.

## Audit compliance (GP-002)

Every state-changing operation in LeaveService (submit, approve, reject, cancel) calls `auditService.record(...)`. BalanceService.deductBalance and restoreBalance also record audit entries. This is wired into the service implementations, not the controller.

## RBAC enforcement (GP-005)

Route handlers apply RBAC middleware stubs (Phase 8). Approve/reject endpoints require manager role. Submit/cancel require employee role. Balance lookup requires authenticated user (employee or manager).

open_questions.question: How should partial-day leave deductions be rounded?
open_questions.impact: Affects deductBalance, restoreBalance, and hasSufficientBalance in the balance module. The rounding rule (nearest half-day, ceiling, floor, or exact decimal) must be consistent across all three methods. If chosen inconsistently, balance checks could pass while deductions fail or vice versa.
candidate_options: Ceiling — always round up to next full day
Floor — always round down to nearest full day
Exact decimal — allow fractional days with no rounding

open_questions.question: How are leave requests spanning two fiscal years handled for balance deduction?
open_questions.impact: Affects deductBalance and hasSufficientBalance. A leave request from Dec 28 – Jan 4 crosses a fiscal year boundary. Should the entire request be deducted from the start-date fiscal year, split proportionally across both years, or rejected if either year has insufficient balance?
candidate_options: Deduct entirely from the fiscal year of the start date
Split days proportionally across both fiscal years
Reject the request if either fiscal year has insufficient balance for its portion

open_questions.question: What are the valid values for LeaveBalance.status?
open_questions.impact: The DOMAIN.md defines status as 'string' with no enumerated values. This field drives balance initialization, accrual logic, and whether a balance can be deducted from. Without defined values, the balance service cannot enforce state transitions.
